query_database.py:181-202. Entry is created and users incremented (185-189) with no await before the try at 191, so no cancellation can land in that gap (only non-cancellation interrupts like KeyboardInterrupt, not an input a caller can produce). Any BaseException from acquire (incl. cancellation) hits 193-196 and calls _release_queue_entry, which deletes the entry when users<=0 (159-161). After acquire, the yield sits in try/finally (198-202) releasing lock and entry, so normal exit, exceptions, and GeneratorExit from aclose of an abandoned context manager all release. The identity check prevents deleting a successor. Waiters are counted in users, so deletion only occurs when nobody holds or awaits. Traced input: cancelled waiter and abandoned CM, neither strands an entry.

query_database.py:151-161 _release_queue_entry deletes only when users<=0 AND the registered entry `is entry`; otherwise it leaves the registry alone, as the doc says. Entries are only created when absent (185-188), so a superseded entry cannot arise on current paths; the guard is defensive and the doc describes its behaviour correctly. Cancelled waiter: line 189 increments users, and the `except BaseException` at 193-196 calls _release_queue_entry before re-raising, so the sole waiter's entry is deleted. Hostile input: a waiter cancelled while a holder is active. The entry stays for the holder, then is deleted at the holder's release (200-202), so nothing accumulates.

query_database.py:185-202 _conversation_turn uses one asyncio.Lock per conversation id; waiters are FIFO, and a cancelled waiter (193-196) just leaves the queue and releases its users count without disturbing others' order. The entry is kept while users>0 (151-161), so no second lock is minted. Baseline length is read after lock acquisition and before send_message (441-462), so nothing the call adds precedes the baseline. CancelledError during the run triggers synchronous _rollback_conversation (468-479) before the lock is released; conversation_store.py:116-123 truncates messages past baseline (including baseline 0 for new conversations). Unqueued path is only conversation_id None, which cannot share a conversation. Claim matches the code.

Criteria file read; criterion 2 present and graded with sibling limits (criterion 3 only serializes same-id calls). query_database.py:165-202 _conversation_turn keys an asyncio.Lock per conversation id in _CONVERSATION_QUEUES (lines 148, 185-192); None id is unqueued (181-183). No global lock on the run path: _AGENT_LOCK (tools/_agent.py:41,64) guards only agent construction, done before the turn (query_database.py:426). Blocking DB calls go through run_blocking_sql (sql_threads.py, SQL_WORKER_THREADS=8, semaphore per loop) in the postgres/mysql/sqlite runners, so two different-id calls can both be in blocking calls at once. Anthropic uses anthropic.AsyncAnthropic (llm.py:72), not a blocking client, so it does not hold the loop. Trigger alternatives split: same-id lock wait -> outside the trigger (claim requires different ids); None id -> outside trigger (no lock); semaphore wait beyond 8 threads -> outside the trigger (needs more than two calls; criterion 10 states the shared pool limit); lock acquire cancellation -> releases entry, outside trigger.

criteria.json read; criterion 3 present and matches the claim. query_database.py:441 `async with _conversation_turn(conversation_id)` wraps baseline read and the whole `agent.send_message` loop (463-497), releasing the lock in the finally at 198-202 (return, failure, or cancel). The lock is a per-id asyncio.Lock (124-148); users counts waiters too, so no second lock is minted for one id (185-189). Messages are appended by the agent during the run inside the lock, so history is first call's messages then second's; test_same_conversation_id_runs_one_at_a_time (test file:157-181) asserts the second turn enters only after the first finishes and that messages == ['first','second']. Split conditions: `conversation_id is None` -> outside the trigger (the claim's trigger is two calls with the same id; None mints a private id nobody can name, and server.py always passes an id). Acquire failure/cancel while waiting -> releases the claim and re-raises, so it does not start a run. Failure and cancel in the run -> lock released in finally, so the next call starts after.

criteria.json read; criterion 4 present and is this claim. In src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py, _conversation_turn (165-202) increments entry.users (189) with no await between lookup/create and increment. Split conditions: (a) conversation_id is None (181) -> outside the trigger: creates no entry at all, so none is held. (b) except BaseException around lock.acquire (193-196) -> releases the user count and re-raises, covering a call cancelled while waiting its turn. (c) finally (200-202) -> releases lock and entry for return, failure, or cancellation while running. _release_queue_entry (151-161) decrements users and deletes the dict entry when users<=0 and the dict still maps to that same entry; users counts holders plus waiters, so the entry survives only while someone is still interested. After the last call finishes the dict entry is gone. Single call site at line 441 uses the context manager. No await between acquire success and the try, so no leak window.

Criteria file counts (criterion 5 present). query_database.py:441-479: inside `async with _conversation_turn(...)`, baseline message count is read after the turn lock is taken (so after earlier calls finished) at 456; the `except asyncio.CancelledError` at 468 calls _rollback_conversation(agent, queued_id, baseline_user_id, baseline_messages) before the lock context exits, then re-raises. _rollback_conversation (223-284) is synchronous and calls store.truncate_messages; conversation_store.py:93-124 does `del conversation.messages[length:]`, dropping only the cancelled call's messages and keeping the first `length`. Next call reads the truncated history. Code condition split: `queued_id is not None` false (no conversation id) -> outside the trigger: no conversation is tracked/persisted by id. Missing/raising truncate_messages on a custom store -> logs ERROR, returns (fault alternative; only for embedder-supplied non-default stores, unreachable with default wiring per the shipped BoundedConversationStore). Conversation not existing at baseline -> length 0, truncates to empty. Evicted conversation -> returns False, nothing to restore. Cancellation while waiting for the turn or during baseline read is not 'while running' (and holds no added messages).

criteria.json read; criterion 6 matches the claim, and criteria 5 and 4 do not narrow it. query_database.py:468-479: `except asyncio.CancelledError` runs the rollback and then a bare `raise`, so no result is returned. Criteria file counts (criterion 7 matches claim). The PR diff touches only query_database.py (turn lock + baseline + cancel rollback), conversation_store.py (new truncate_messages), docs and tests. It does not touch the Anthropic client, streaming or non-streaming paths, components_to_blocks, or _meta assembly. criteria.json counted (criterion 9 present). Runners call cursor.fetchmany(effective_row_cap(self._max_rows)+1) (postgres sql_runner.py:179-180, mysql :148-149, sqlite :151-152). effective_row_cap (safety/limits.py:36-54) returns min(constructor_cap, effective.max_rows) from the contextvar, so a lower profile max_rows gives profile max_rows+1. The change moves the driver work onto worker threads via run_blocking_sql (sql_threads.py:146), which runs func under contextvars.copy_context().run, so the profile contextvar is still visible in the worker and the cap is preserved. Trigger split: effective is None -> outside trigger (no profile bound); profile max_rows >= base -> outside trigger (not lower). No departure found. RowCapRunner also trims post-fetch.

Criteria file counts (criterion 10 present). The criterion says 'It adds no thread pool of its own. Anthropic calls and database queries share asyncio's default executor'. In the head view, src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sql_threads.py:8-22,77-91 runs SQL driver work on a dedicated ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8, thread_name_prefix='sqllens-sql') behind an asyncio.Semaphore, explicitly 'separate from the event loop's default executor'. So database queries do not share the default executor. This pool is not in this PR's diff (diff touches only changelog, docs tools.md, conversation_store.py, query_database.py, tests), but it is in the head and contradicts the claimed state. Other parts (ChromaDB 2-thread pool at chromadb/agent_memory.py:125, no interruption of running threads) match. Also, the dedicated pool means 'further calls wait for a free thread' on a different limit (8 slots, 60s timeout then SqlWorkersBusyError).
